```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Everything that is specific to an instrument is described in one YAML file,
read with `read_instrument()`. This vignette lists every key. Defaults are
given in brackets; keys without a default are required.

A complete small example is `inst/instruments/demo7/demo7.yml`:

```{r, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
cat(readLines(system.file("instruments/demo7/demo7.yml", package = "normpipe")), sep = "\n")
```

## Top level

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | short identifier of the instrument, used in file names |
| `name` | display name [`id`] |
| `report_step` | reporting step for scales with a dense set of attainable scores (see `mean_of_means`) [0.01] |
| `items` | item table (below) |
| `versions` | list of versions, each with its scales (below) |
| `cells` | reporting cells and continuous-age settings (below) |
| `uncertainty` | settings of the norm bands and intervals (below) |
| `measurement` | calibration of the item models (below) |
| `transfer` | optional transfer module (below) |
| `weighting` | raking of the reference weights (below) |

YAML 1.1 reads the bare keys `n`, `y`, `no`, `yes`, `off`, `on` as booleans,
so the number of items is given as `n_items`, not `n`.

## `items`

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n_items` | number of items; item ids are then `1, ..., n_items` |
| `ids` | alternatively, an explicit vector of integer item ids |
| `prefix` | column name prefix in the data: item 5 is column `<prefix>5` [`"item_"`] |
| `categories` | response codes as they appear in the data, from low to high [`[0, 1, 2, 3]`] |
| `values` | score value of each category [`0, 1, ..., K - 1`] |
| `unit` | all values must be multiples of `unit` (e.g. 0.5 for half points) [1] |
| `reverse` | ids of reverse-keyed items (their values are reversed) |
| `overrides` | list of `{items: [...], categories: [...], values: [...], reverse: true/false}` for items with a different format |

Values must be non-negative. Non-uniform values are allowed, e.g.
`values: [2, 1, 0, 1, 2]` for a bipolar item scored as distance from the
midpoint. Item models always run on the categories ordered by value, so
reverse-keyed items keep a positive slope. Every configured category must
occur in the calibration data; collapse empty categories here.

## `versions`

Each version has an `id`, an optional `label` and a list of `scales`.
Outcomes are named `<version id>_<scale id>`.

| Scale key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | scale identifier, unique within the version |
| `label` | display label [`id`] |
| `level` | free label used in the exports, e.g. `facet`, `domain`, `total` [`"scale"`] |
| `items` | item ids of the scale |
| `components` | instead of `items`: earlier scales of the same version (by `id`) or inline `{id, items}` lists |
| `metric` | `sum` (sum of item values), `mean` (sum / number of items), or `mean_of_means` (mean of the component means; needs `components`) [`mean`] |
| `model` | `grm`, `bifactor`, `composite` or `none` [`grm` without components, `bifactor` with components] |
| `calibrate_from` | outcome whose item model is used instead of fitting one, e.g. `full_a` for a short form scored with the long-form item parameters |
| `equal_block_slopes` | `true`: specific slopes are constrained equal within each block of a bifactor model (needed for two-item blocks) |
| `min_answered` | proportion of the items that must be answered for a prorated score [1] |
| `observed` | `true`/`false` forces the direct or the transfer route; otherwise the route follows from the items present in the reference data |

The attainable raw scores follow from the item values by convolution. A
`mean_of_means` scale whose components differ in length (or in their value
sets) has a dense set of attainable scores and is tabulated on a grid with
step `report_step`.

Models:

- `grm`: unidimensional graded response model of the scale's items.
- `bifactor`: general factor plus one specific factor per component.
- `composite`: total scores; every component must also be a scale of the
  same version with an item model (fitted or via `calibrate_from`). The components are coupled by a
  second-order structure whose loadings are estimated from the component
  scores of the calibration data.
- `none`: norms and norm bands only, no individual intervals.

## `cells`

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `gender` | gender codes that form reporting cells, as in `meta$gender` (omit for no gender cells) |
| `age_breaks` | breaks of the age bands, closed on the left; `Inf` (or `.inf`) for an open upper band (omit for no age bands) |
| `ages` | `[from, to]`: range of integer ages for continuous-age norms (omit to skip stage `M3b`) |
| `overall` | also compute the overall table [`true`] |
| `kernel` | continuous-age kernel: `half_width0` [4], `min_neff` [150], `max_half_width` [12] |

The reporting cells are all combinations of the configured gender codes and
age bands. For continuous-age norms an Epanechnikov kernel around every
target age starts at `half_width0` years and widens by one year until the
local effective sample size reaches `min_neff`, up to `max_half_width`.

## `uncertainty`

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prior_mass` | effective number of pseudo-observations per reporting cell, spread uniformly over the attainable scores; 0 switches the prior off [1] |
| `n_boot` | number of Bayesian-bootstrap draws for the norm bands [200] |
| `n_param_draws` | number of item-parameter draws for the integrated intervals [50] |
| `probs` | lower and upper quantile of bands and intervals [`[0.025, 0.975]`] |
| `pctl_clamp` | percentile ranks are clamped to `[pctl_clamp, 1 - pctl_clamp]` before the T transformation [1e-4] |
| `pctl_convention` | `midpoint` or `cumulative` [`midpoint`] |

Percentile conventions:

- `midpoint`: PR = P(X < x) + ½ P(X = x), the classical percentile rank. Its
  mean over the norm sample is exactly 50, and the lowest score is not
  shifted upwards by the mass at that score.
- `cumulative`: PR = P(X ≤ x), the relative cumulative frequency. Use it to
  reproduce tables that were built with this convention.

T = 50 + 10 Φ⁻¹(PR) in both cases.

## `measurement`

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `engine` | `auto` (mirt when installed, otherwise the built-in estimator), `mirt`, or `internal` [`auto`] |

The item models are calibrated in the reference sample unless
`run_norming()` gets a separate calibration sample (`calib`) or pre-fitted
models (`models`). With mirt, a model whose Oakes information matrix cannot
be inverted is refitted with a tighter EM tolerance and, if necessary, with
the cross-product information; check `model$info$converged` for weakly
identified bifactor models. The built-in estimator (penalised marginal
maximum likelihood) needs no further package but is slow for long scales.

## `weighting`

Used when `run_norming()` receives population `margins`. A margin is a data
frame with one or more raking variables and a column `Freq` (population
counts); a list of such data frames is raked jointly, e.g. age band ×
gender from `make_margins()` plus a separate education margin
(`data.frame(education = ..., Freq = ...)`, with `education` a column of
`ref$meta`).

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `trim_quantile` | raked weights are capped at this quantile; 1 switches trimming off [0.99] |
| `rerake` | rake again after trimming, and trim again, until the margins hold and no weight exceeds the cap [true] |
| `incomplete` | respondents with a missing raking variable (or a gender outside the cells): `drop`, or `keep` them with their design weight rescaled to the raked total, so that they enter the overall norms [`drop`] |

`rerake: false` reproduces the one-shot trimming of normpipe 0.1.0.

## `missing`

How single items that a respondent of the reference sample skipped are
handled. Who is in the sample of a scale is decided beforehand and
independently by `min_answered` of the scale.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reference` | `prorate`: scores are computed from the answered items. `impute`: every skipped item is drawn from its distribution in the reference sample given the answered items of its block, in `n_imputations` completed data sets (`impute_items()`) [`prorate`] |
| `n_imputations` | number of completed data sets [20] |

With `impute`, all scores of the reference sample come from the completed
items: the directly normed scales, the bridge predictors of the transfer
models and the observed part of the transfer outcomes. Draw `r` of a draw
frame uses completed data set `((r - 1) mod M) + 1`, so the spread between
the imputations enters the norm bands. The block of an item is the bridge
predictor that contains it, otherwise the shortest scale that contains it;
the conditioning value is the rounded mean of the answered other items of the
block. Transfer fits are not affected (they use the donor samples), so a
change of this setting only requires the frames and norm tables to be
recomputed. The calibration of the measurement models uses the items as
answered.

## `transfer`

The transfer module (stage `M2`) is needed only when the reference sample
did not answer all items of some scales.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | switch the module on [`false`] |
| `bridge` | list of bridge predictors `{id, items}`: item sets answered by the reference sample and the donor samples; each enters as its mean item value |
| `formula` | right-hand side of the mean model; `{bridge}` stands for the bridge predictors [`"{bridge} + s(age) + gender + sample"`]; e.g. `"{bridge} + s(age, by = gender) + gender + sample"` for gender-specific age trajectories |
| `sigma` | right-hand side of the sigma model [`"br_mean + s(age)"`] |
| `family` | likelihood of the transfer model [`gaussian`], or a list of candidates (e.g. `[beta_binomial, gaussian]`) among which the stage chooses per outcome by PSIS-LOO among the converged fits (`m2_family_selection.csv`): `gaussian` or `skew_normal` are latent distributions of an interval-censored likelihood on the attainable scores; `beta_binomial` models the summed score as a count out of the attainable range, with a logit mean model and a precision model `phi`; dense scales (e.g. means of facet means) keep a censored family via `outcomes` |
| `phi` | right-hand side of the precision model of the beta-binomial [same as `sigma`] |
| `reference_level` | donor sample used as the reference level of `sample` in the fit [first level of `meta$sample`] |
| `projection_level` | level of `sample` at which the reference sample is projected: a donor sample, or `average` (mean of the sample effects) [`reference_level`] |
| `bootstrap_weights` | Bayesian bootstrap of the reference weights in every posterior draw, so that the norm band also reflects the sampling error of the reference sample [true] |
| `exclude` | per outcome, bridge ids left out of the predictors, e.g. `{full_x: [a2]}` |
| `crosscheck` | directly observed outcomes that are additionally projected without their own bridge items (leave-own-domain-out); results in `c1_crosscheck.csv` |
| `outcomes` | per-outcome overrides of `formula`, `sigma`, `phi`, `family`, `exclude`, `adapt_delta`, `max_treedepth`, `chains`, `iter`, `prior_b`, `prior_b_phi`, `priors`, `init`, `select_rhat` |
| `n_draws` | posterior predictive draws per reference respondent [500] |
| `adapt_delta`, `max_treedepth` | sampler settings passed to brms [0.95, 10] |
| `chains`, `iter` | number of chains and iterations per chain [4, 2000] |
| `prior_b` | prior of the regression coefficients of the mean model [`normal(0, 1)`; `normal(0, 1.5)` on the logit scale of the beta-binomial] |
| `prior_b_phi` | prior of the coefficients of log(phi) of the beta-binomial [`normal(0, 2.5)`] |
| `select_rhat` | largest R-hat of a candidate family that may be chosen [1.01] |
| `priors` | further brms priors as a list of `{prior, class, dpar, coef}`; an entry replaces a default of the same class, dpar and coef, e.g. `[{prior: "normal(0, 0.5)", class: b, dpar: sigma}]` [none] |
| `init` | initial values: `random` (brms default) or `0`; left out, the family default is used [beta-binomial: 0; censored families: intercepts at the location and log scale of the outcome, all else 0] |
| `backend` | `cmdstanr` or `rstan` [cmdstanr when CmdStan is installed, otherwise rstan] |

The donor samples are attached to the instrument object before calling
`run_norming()`:

```r
inst$donors_data <- list(meta = donor_meta, items = donor_items)
```

`donor_meta` needs `id`, `age`, `gender` and `sample`. For every scale that
needs the transfer, a Bayesian distributional regression predicts the scale
score, by default from the bridge scores, `s(age)`, `gender` and `sample`,
with an interval-censored normal likelihood and `sigma` depending on the mean
bridge score and `s(age)`.

Bridge items that belong to the outcome are observed in the reference sample
and are never predicted, whatever the family: the model describes only the
part of the outcome that is not observed (the outcome minus the weighted
observed items in the donor samples; for the beta-binomial the sum of the
unobserved items out of their range), and the projection adds each reference
respondent's observed part to every posterior predictive draw of the rest.
The rest carries the parameter and residual uncertainty, the observed part is
data. An observed item the respondent skipped is drawn anew in every draw from
its distribution in the donor samples given the answered item of the same
bridge pair; with `missing: {reference: impute}` it is taken from the
completed data sets instead, like every other skipped item. That observed
items are never predicted is fixed; it has no switch.

The posterior predictive draws for the reference
sample, evaluated at the projection level of `sample` and combined with
Bayesian-bootstrap weights, form the draw frame of the scale. Reference
respondents without age, or with a gender category that does not occur in
the donor samples, cannot be projected and are left out of the transfer
scales. With cmdstanr, CmdStan must be installed
(`cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()`).

To reproduce norms built with normpipe 0.1.0, set `bootstrap_weights: false`.

A small example is `inst/instruments/demo7/demo7_transfer.yml`; a large one
with 17 two-item bridge predictors is `inst/instruments/pid5/pid5.yml`.
